title: Dual-contract MGDA matched offline training smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Replacing the ordinary decision-weighted opponent-seat policy gradient with a norm-matched minimum-norm common-descent direction will prevent the known locally harmful group update and improve cross-anchor breadth without violating the frozen Standard10 base or residual cap.
material_change: From the exact same zero-residual state and immutable 4,096-hand cohort, train control and treatment for 32 identical stratified update steps. Both use the same sampled rows, fixed within-group advantages, Adam, value loss, entropy, clipping, and policy-gradient norm. Control uses ordinary decision-share aggregation; treatment uses minimum-norm convex aggregation of six unit policy gradients. Freeze both and evaluate 1,024 untouched mirrored pairs against each of three learned anchors.
baseline: Exact-parent gradient audit found 4 materially negative pairwise cosines, ordinary worst group alignment -0.1708, and robust worst alignment +0.5039. Prior group-RMS policy-level delta was pooled -0.504 CI[-16.184,15.176], with only Slumbot-free positive.
notes: This is an offline mechanism/efficacy smoke using existing training evidence and untouched evaluation decks. Admission to independent new-hand multi-seed replication requires treatment-control point delta >0 on at least 2/3 anchors, pooled >0, Standard10 >=0, both pooled seats >=0, exact initial/base identity, identical sampled rows/update counts, cap <=0.25, and robust positive worst-group alignment on at least 75% of steps. Failure without broad regression is inconclusive at this scale; broad directional regression plus loss of the gradient mechanism rejects this formulation only.

Independent raw recomputation confirmed 3,072 pairs / 12,288 hands, evidence SHA256 bd570b2c32d4683028e4198f7898b01adffff0a0361f11df6db3c2f3afab6121, pooled delta +0.559408 bb/100 and 95% CI [-15.776789,16.895604].

result.summary: MGDA retained strictly positive worst-group policy-gradient alignment on all 32/32 steps, whereas ordinary aggregation was locally harmful on many steps. On 12,288 new common-deck evaluation hands, treatment-control pooled +0.559 bb/100 CI[-15.777,16.896], but only CFR96 improved (+13.640); Standard10 (-3.833), Slumbot-free (-8.129), and pooled seat1 (-0.960) were negative.
result.conclusion: The conflict-aware mechanism survived training and avoided the audited local gradient defect, but this single small offline cohort did not demonstrate broad policy improvement. Because the pooled point is nonnegative and no catastrophic drift occurred, this is insufficient-evidence at 4k lineage hands rather than a scale-independent rejection. It does not meet the preregistered gate for spending new environment hands.
result.next_step: Before collecting new hands, run one independent-seed replication on the already-existing immutable 4,096-hand dual-contract reward-smoke cohort with the same 32-step matched protocol and new untouched evaluation decks. Promote to modest new-hand multi-seed scaling only if breadth and Standard10 preservation replicate or a geometric learning curve supports it.
